rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Epistemic mood is not punitive mood
rules_evaluated.evidence: M1's contracted mood is joyful creation, not unease, so the epistemic-vs-punitive test doesn't apply. Checked for accidental shame anyway: 'All learners... everyone struggles to keep up' (line 24) normalizes difficulty collectively, and 'The agent's self-report is a hypothesis, not ground truth' (line 59) frames the introspection discipline as a fact about the tool, not a student failing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode
rules_evaluated.evidence: New Big Idea (lines 5-6) leads with 'leave something behind,' a positive discipline (compounding), not a failure word — 'no compounding' names the negative case the discipline addresses, in the compendium's own approved shape, not the title. What You'll Learn (lines 15-20) leads every bullet with a positive-discipline verb: Run, Distinguish, Fix, Close, Compound. Key Concepts (lines 57-63) open on the loop, context, the agent's self-report, a failing test, the rules file, and tracker conventions — none on a failure noun.

File keeps M1's four-exercise order (orient → fix → close → compound; maintainer block line 96 restates 'compound sits last... close sits third,' matching the doc). 'no plan mode' survives in the What You'll Learn bullet (line 18), matching the doc's deliberate M1 restraint. No Skill/subagent language appears anywhere, matching 'No Skill use at M1.' The new Willison pre-read paragraph in Prework (line 12) mirrors the doc's reading-in-two-places rule for the M1→M2 gap rather than front-running it. 'Next' (lines 65-66) and the M2 pre-reads (68-78) name M2's destination only at signposting level ('a second pass that pressure-tests the plan') — it never names the walk-down-branches/grill-me mechanic the strategy doc reserves for M2's own Skill-adjacent reveal, so M2's teaching moment isn't front-run.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts
rules_evaluated.evidence: Key Concepts (lines 57-63) instance at least four of the doc's stated M1 themes: compounding (loop bullet + CLAUDE.local.md bullet), self-aware/grain-of-salt + mirror (the self-report-as-hypothesis bullet), 90%-correct (the /context unread-slice bullet), and capture-your-world (the tracker-conventions bullet). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Key Concepts shape — theme breadcrumbs, not standalone section
rules_evaluated.evidence: All six Key Concepts bullets (lines 57-63) recap moves the four exercises already ran (emergent), pass §3/§4/§5 first, carry no bold 'Remember:' label or standalone themes section. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: What You'll Learn shape — capability register, not syllabus
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lines 15-20 are five engineer-readable capability bullets — Run, Distinguish, Fix, Close, Compound — each with a concrete object (the loop, the agent's account vs. the repo, the bug + PR, the ticket, the rules file at ./CLAUDE.local.md).
